Letter, Johan Gottlieb Kolbe to his son, 23 August 1830

National Library of South Africa, MSB 751, the G. A. Kolbe Collection, Special Collections, Cape Town. Four pages from the London tailor to his son at the Cape. The catalogue calls it a letter written on his ordination and it is not — it reports the son being “fully accepted by the [L.M.S.] as one of their Missionaries”, which is the acceptance and not the ordination. Read at full resolution from the supplied PDFs on 20 September 2026. The letter →
Dictionary of South African Biography — the entry on George Augustus Kolbe

Typescript by Karel Schoeman, dated February 1992 and headed voorlopige teks (provisional text), supplied by Melanie Geustyn of the NLSA. The DSAB was terminated after Volume V in 1987, five years before this was written, so on the published record this typescript is the only form the entry has ever taken. Nine of its statements agree with documents held here; two are demonstrably wrong. Read and tested →
Sibree, A Register of Missionaries (LMS, 1923)

James Sibree's register of every London Missionary Society missionary. Found free and complete, and it carries Kolbe's whole mission life in one entry. It also settles a question this archive had left open: Mr Miles was the officer who accepted him, not a messenger carrying somebody else's decision. The entry →
The Mirror of Literature, Amusement, and Instruction, Vol. XIV (1829), pp. 313–318

“SPIRIT OF THE PUBLIC JOURNALS — A SINGULAR LETTER FROM SOUTHERN AFRICA. Communicated by Mr. Hogg, the Ettrick Shepherd.” The story the tailor asked his son to verify in 1830. It is fiction by James Hogg, printed as a settler's letter home — so the tailor's scepticism was right and the son was never expected to confirm it. Read from the Internet Archive, item s1id13414270. The story →

sections.title: Estate and archival references in hand

rows.h: KAB: MOOC 6/9/35: 7698 (1845)
Estate of George Augustus Kolbe, d. 1 December 1844 at the farm "Wurtemburg", Colesberg district. Cape Archives, Master's Office. Not yet ordered.
SAG "b3"
The generation code recorded against Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe at her 1846 marriage — a pointer into the published Suid-Afrikaanse Geslagsregisters. Not yet followed.
KAB: MOOC 6/9/21: 4393 (1840)

Death notice of JAMES MONTJOY, saddler, d. Cradock September 1827. Read in full — located at image 338 of 2,223 on film 007844936 by interpolating reference numbers, since it is not name-indexed. Line 3, the parents: "Not Known." Transcribed →
KAB: MOOC 7/1/268: 87 (1845)

Will of JOHANNA CATHARINA MONTJOY, wife of Petrus Jacobus Booysen. Made eighteen years before her death. Cannot be located on film. Not name-indexed, and every nineteenth-century Cape film whose target board this archive has read says DEATH NOTICES — the separate wills volumes are not evidently in the collection. The catalogue would settle it and is blocked. The attempt →
KAB: MOOC 6/9/—: 6167 (1843)

Death notice of JOHANNA BOOYZEN, born about 1754, widow of Charles du Plessis, of 28 Roze Street, Cape Town. Read in full. NOT this family, and read precisely because her dates match the only two this archive has for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer. Transcribed →
KAB: MOOC 6/9/104: 499 (1863)
Death notice of JOHANNA CATHARINA BOOYSEN née MONTJOY, d. 19 May 1863 at Zevenfontein, Brak River. Read in full — names her parents, her eight children and her age to the day. Transcribed →
KAB: MOOC 13/1/221: 6 (1866)

Liquidation and distribution account for the same estate — it would divide an 1863 estate among eight children and give them their married surnames. Cannot be located on film, for the same reason as the will above.
KAB: 84992 (1943)

Death notice of ISABELLA FREDRIKA BOOYZEN, born COETZEE — wife of Gert Jacobus. Read in full. She died 31 March 1930 and the notice was filed thirteen years later; this archive had been using the filing year as her death date. Spelled BOOYZEN by the Master's office throughout. Transcribed →
KAB: MOOC 6/9/5047: 58379 (1938)

Estate papers, JAMES JOHN MOUNTJOY — James Jonathan, retired builder, d. 22 December 1937, Barkly East. Read in full, and not only the death notice — the first and final liquidation account and the distribution account as well, on film 007735716 images 767–770. His wife Maria Louisa Bertha née Kumm is the next file, 58380, as this page predicted; read too. Transcribed →
KAB: MOOC 6/9/15220: 3786/48 (1948)
Estate papers, a second JAMES JOHN MOUNTJOY — the son baptised 30 May 1895.
KAB: MOOC 7/1/104: 42 (1818)

WILL of JAMES MOUNTJOY, joint with SLIER, ANNA CATHARINA, his wife — made a year after their marriage. Requested from the Cape Town Archives, 10 September 2026. The likeliest surviving document to state where he came from.
KAB: MOOC 7/1/104: 43 (1827)
The same pair again, in the year he died. Requested.
KAB: CO 3972: 17 (1834)
Colonial Office memorial — "the widow of J Mountjoy, requesting remission of a fine". A petition in Anna Catharina's own voice, seven years widowed. Requested.
Mortgage bonds, George Mountjoy (1905, 1908) and James John Mountjoy (1908) — the Mountjoy cousins raising money on land in the years the Booyzens had none.
Five mortgage bonds in the name RICHARD PETER BARRY, spanning the war — corroboration for the Cape Rebel of Jerpoint, not proof.
FamilySearch film 007844477

The Master of the Supreme Court's own index of death notices, 1834–1912 — surname, christian name, notice number and year, 612 images. Read at the "Beer, de" pages (278–280) and the Booysen pages (436 onward). Particles index separately, so de Beer files under B.

sections.title: The Transvaal, before anyone thought this family was there
sections.dek: Three notices found by reading a surname rather than chasing a reference. The first of them is the oldest document in this archive.

rows.h:
Sterfkennis 678
Transvaal, Weeskamer
Petrus Jacobus Booijsen — generation six, b. Graaff-Reinet c. 1788
Read Parents named: Gerthardus Lödewikus Booijsen and Magdalena de Beer. Eight children. Nothing to leave. Transcribed →
Sterfkennis 6332
Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier — b. district Cradock c. 1823

Read, and she is kin Died Brakfontein, district Rustenburg — the family farm. Parents Ocken Johannes Oliefier and Anna Johanna Botha. The first wife of Hendrik Stefanus Booijsen, with seven children. Filed here for a week as born Alberts, at Boekfontein, kinship unproven; both readings were wrong.
Sterfkennis 44420
Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen — b. c. 1860
Read, kinship unproven Died Vaalbank, district Lichtenburg. Father entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen.
